transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-09-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Avery Chen (Redwood CSM); Dr. Elena Vargas (Cerulean Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Platform Eng), Sasha Ortiz (CTO), Tina Park (SRE)
---
00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes, so we'll run through the lab results then triage the deltas vs your baseline, sound good?
00:18 Elena: yep that works, thanks Jordan. quick note, Sasha has to hop at 35 minutes, but we can cover the key items first.
00:32 Jordan: perfect. Priya do you want to take us into the numbers?
00:36 Priya: yeah absolutely. so quick context — we re-ran the sprint-6 workload you provided, same prompt mix, same token budgets. we tested on Redwood Dedicated variant and also the hosted flow for contrast. median latency p50 we saw around 110ms for the canonical chat prompt, which is in-line with BaselineCo's median at ~120ms — so good there.
01:02 Marcus: wait you said dedicated and hosted — which was this run? dedicated?
01:06 Priya: this run was on a dedicated slot with batch sizing tuned to your request profile; we also did a hosted pass, results similar for median but a few ms diffs.
01:18 Elena: ok, baseline median's a little higher so that's encouraging. what's the p95 and p99 look like? that's where we saw trouble last week.
01:28 Priya: right. p95 for us is 420ms versus baseline 350ms — so we're worse there. p99 spikes to 1.8s for certain long-context prompts; baseline stayed near 1.1s. the main signal is the tail for long-context where our KV cache warmup and continuous-batch interactions produce variability.
01:52 Jordan: just to be explicit — those long-context prompts are the transcript-rewrite style? the 4k+ context ones?
01:58 Elena: yes, and also the multi-turn clinical note collate flow. we hit p99 in the field and it's sensitive.
02:06 Priya: one datapoint — when we force KV-cache warm caches (i.e., repeated prefixes) the tail collapses substantially to ~650ms p99. so caching helps, but cold or varied prefixes still have tail issues.
02:26 Marcus: can you remind us how your routing works — like if you see a long context is there automatic fallback to a smaller model?
02:33 Priya: yeah we have policy routing. for this pilot we left routing conservative: route-by-latency threshold and seq-len threshold. we did not force fallback to smaller model because we wanted apples-to-apples vs baseline. if we enable fallback for long contexts, tail comes down but you trade fidelity.
02:50 Sasha: hmm fidelity is a concern for us, clinical accuracy matters. can't sacrifice there without evals.
02:55 Jordan: understood. we can run a fidelity-preserving fallback — run rerank + constrained decoding or an eval set to quantify.
03:05 Elena: please. also curious about throughput — we saw your throughput numbers look higher, but we need sustained QPS under bursts. can you break steady vs burst?
03:15 Priya: sure. sustained throughput at 500ms SLA-equivalent was about 120 req/s on the dedicated pool; baseline does ~95 req/s under same config. under a 30s burst (x3 QPS) we saw degraded p95 and some queued requests causing 500ms+ responses, but throughput remained higher overall. queueing policy and autoscale aggressiveness matter.
03:41 Tina: autoscale — did you hit capacity cliffs? how fast were you able to scale?
03:45 Priya: on dedicated we have fast burst capacity but autoscale operates on short windows; we saw an initial cliff ~8-12s while new slots come online. for mission critical we can pre-warm burst capacity or reserve burst tokens.
04:02 Marcus: the baseline provider claims near-zero cold start due to warm pool. can you match that?
04:08 Jordan: we can approximate with reserved burst but it costs; we'll put pricing tradeoffs in the follow-up.
04:14 Elena: ok. any anomalies in error rates or tokenization differences? we had a few hallucination flags last week.
04:20 Priya: error rates were low, <0.05% 5xxs, mostly due to user payloads exceeding max length. tokenization differences are minor — sometimes stop token handling varied which we can align via decoding params. hallucination concern is more model-specific; if you want we can lock to an earlier model variant or run conservative decoding.
04:46 Marcus: did you also try quantized builds? last call you mentioned a quantize-v2 that might change tail.
04:51 Priya: yes; we did a quick experimental pass with quantize-v2 (int8-ish path). that reduced median by ~10ms and p95 by ~40ms in steady state, but in some long-context cases the p99 still had spikes — looks like kernel scheduling jitter interacts with KV lookups in that path.
05:14 Jordan: so quantize helps cost and median, but not a silver bullet for tail. next step is a tuned quantize profile plus some batch policy tweaks.
05:23 Elena: what's the expected unit cost delta vs baseline on quantized?
05:28 Jordan: rough numbers — quantized reduces inference token cost ~18-22% vs our non-quantized baseline. versus BaselineCo depends on their infra; we'll itemize in pricing doc.
05:38 Sasha: any security or compliance changes with quantization or dedicated? we need assurances on model artifact handling.
05:45 Avery: from a customer side we keep key management and logs within your VPC if you use Redwood Private; quantization doesn't change data residency — models run in the same perimeter. we can share SOC2 and the whitepaper on KMS/HSM integration after.
06:02 Tina: perfect, please send. also note our legal wants audit logs for inference payload sampling turned on. how heavy is that for performance?
06:12 Priya: minimal, logs are async and batched; negligible for median but does add I/O overhead on heavy bursts. we'll quantify in the follow-up.
06:26 Marcus: returning to routing — what tuning knobs do we have to reduce tail while preserving accuracy?
06:31 Priya: options: (1) enable fallback to a trimmed model for long context with post-rerank; (2) increase prefix caching TTLs and bias batch scheduling to favor cached KV hits; (3) tuned batching windows — narrower windows reduce latency variance but lower throughput; (4) pre-warmed burst slots; (5) custom kernel config for long-seq execution (we have an alternate kernel selection setting).
07:05 Elena: can you do (2) and (3) first — caching and smaller batching window — low risk.
07:11 Priya: yes, we can push a caching TTL change and reduce batch window from 40ms to 20ms for your profile in the lab. that should reduce some p95 variance.
07:20 Marcus: what's the expected p95 improvement if you do that?
07:23 Priya: ballpark — p95 down from 420ms to ~330-360ms for mixed workloads. p99 improvement depends on cache warm fraction.
07:33 Jordan: we'll run a tuned pass and share results in 48 hours. Elena, you asked about fidelity-preserving fallback — we'll run a small eval set to measure delta on clinical tasks.
07:44 Elena: great. any other surprises from the logs? latency correlation with token-length had a small bimodal distribution — some 2xx token requests were slower than longer ones, odd.
07:56 Priya: noted — that's likely due to batching skews and when network serialization happens; we'll check request timing traces and share sample spans.
08:06 Tina: make sure to include trace IDs when you send traces so our SRE can map to our observability.
08:12 Priya: will do.
08:16 Jordan: quick commercial note — if you want to lock dedicated slots we can offer a 3-month pilot with reduced slot pricing and a burst reserve knob to mimic baseline warm pools.
08:27 Sasha: what's the delta in $/req we should expect for reserved vs burst-on-demand?
08:32 Jordan: initial estimate — reserved reduces per-request GPU cost ~12-18% depending on utilization; burst reserve adds fixed monthly but reduces peak tail by enabling instant capacity. I'll send a simple calc sheet.
08:45 Marcus: for our procurement path, we need a piece of paper showing expected cost at 50% and 80% utilization.
08:51 Jordan: we'll include 50/80 utilization scenarios in the follow-up.
08:56 Elena: ok if we map next steps — Priya tuning, Marcus logs, Jordan pricing, Tina confirm VPC egress — satisfied?
09:04 Sasha: yes, proceed.
09:07 Jordan: excellent. we'll schedule a 60-min deep-dive on routing next week. anything else?
09:13 Elena: one small ask — can you run a head-to-head where you enable fallback to smaller model with rerank and show latency/fidelity tradeoff?
09:20 Priya: yes we can — we'll include rerank eval metrics and playback examples.
09:25 Jordan: great. thanks everyone.
---
End of call.
